name: Lehman 2016 gamer pairs: Thomas 20+2, then Burst-X 20-2 (22 min)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Lehman 2016, MSc thesis, ch. 4), 8-solenoid circumcerebral ring
summary: Lehman's 2016 thesis session for two video-game players 10 m apart sharing one field: 4 min without field, 6 min of the Thomas pattern on an accelerating counter-clockwise rotation (20 down to 6 ms per coil), 8 min of Burst-X on a decelerating one (20 up to 34 ms), then 4 min without field. The thesis reports no difference between field and no-field run times for all players combined.
notes: Lehman 2016: 11 two-minute runs of the game Super Hexagon: 2 baseline runs without field, 3 with 'the accelerating pattern', 4 with 'the decelerating pattern', 2 baseline runs (p.67 [58]). Both rings were connected to the same Intel 286 computer (p.65 [56]); sessions were synchronised between players with a stopwatch (p.67 [58]). The methods define only the 20-2 rotation and do not say which waveform ran in which rotation (p.65-67 [56-58]). Thomas with 20+2 and Burst-X with 20-2 is this project's inference from the labels T and B in Fig. 4.4 and from the discussion (p.69-71 [60-62]). The Thomas pattern plays from the 849-point patent table at 1 ms per point (the lab's file had 839 or 859 points). The Burst-X point values were never published; the project's rising sweep stands in, 230 points of 1 ms. Both repeat back to back, counter-clockwise from Fp1 to Fp2; the site names are this project's reading. One helmet delivers one of the two exposures, so both players run this program, started together. The thesis measured 1 to 5 uT along the inside of each solenoid (p.66 [57]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1.5 uT that is about 84 uT at the coil face and 36 uT at the scalp, more at the surface than in the original. Lehman (7 men) found no field against no-field difference in run times for all players combined. Experienced players in the field group scored higher during Burst-X (p = .01) but also lower in the baseline before any field was on. Thesis data, small sample, never replicated. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Two players, each wearing a helmet running this program, started together (the original drove both rings from one Intel 286 computer). Each sits with a laptop on the lap, facing north or south, one in a shielded acoustic chamber (Faraday cage) and one in a darkened room 10 m away, playing Super Hexagon on "hard". An assistant calls a new run every 2 min (every 30 s for novices); the player calls out the run time after each death and forces a death at 2 min.
schedule: One 22-min session per trial (pairs ran 1-4 trials). Lehman's control pairs played the same session with no field; for a self-test use the app's Blind option and fix the comparison in advance.
source: Lehman 2016, Interaction between virtual (computer gaming) environments, brain activity, and the Schumann resonance as the next evolutionary step in adaptation: Teilhard de Chardin's noosphere, MSc thesis (Biology), Laurentian University, ch. 4 https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Juden-Kelly, Dotta, Vares & Persinger 2015, J Conscious Explor Res 6(9):728-737 (Thomas primer at 20+2, Burst-X effector at 20-2, 1-ms points) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/497 ; Dotta & Persinger 2012, J Biophys Chem 3:72-80 https://file.scirp.org/Html/17181.html ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
